chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Everyone who professes religion to God Mighty and Majestic through worship in which he exerts his soul, and has no Imam for him from God — his striving is unaccepted, and he is straying and confused, and God abhors his deeds.

His likeness is like the likeness of a sheep that strayed from its shepherd and its herd. It wandered going and coming all day. When the night enveloped it, it saw a herd of sheep with their shepherd; it yearned toward them and was deceived by them and spent the night with them in their pen. When the shepherd drove his herd, it did not recognize its shepherd or its herd, and it wandered confusedly seeking its shepherd and its herd. Then it saw another flock with their shepherd and yearned toward them and was deceived by them. The shepherd called out to it: Go back to your shepherd and your herd — for you are wandering and confused away from your shepherd and your herd! So it fled, frightened and bewildered, with no shepherd to guide it to its pasture or return it. While it was in this state, the wolf seized upon its being lost and devoured it.

And likewise, by God, O Muhammad, anyone from this community who begins the morning without an Imam from God Mighty and Majestic — manifest and just — begins the morning straying and wandering. And if he dies in this state, he dies the death of disbelief and hypocrisy. Know, O Muhammad, that the tyrannous imams and their followers are truly cut off from the religion of God. They have gone astray and led others astray. Thus the deeds which they perform are like ashes blown fiercely by the wind on a stormy day — they cannot hold on to anything from what they have earned. That is the far straying.'

key_terms.أئمة الجور: Tyrannous imams — illegitimate rulers who usurped authority
key_terms.إمام من الله: Imam from God — the divinely designated Imam, distinct from self-appointed leaders
key_terms.الضلال البعيد: The far straying — total and irreversible misguidance
key_terms.دان الله: To profess religion to God, to take as one's religion — implies outward, sincere practice
key_terms.سعيه غير مقبول: His striving is unaccepted — the doctrine that worship without valid Imamate is rejected
key_terms.شانئ: Abhors — God's active rejection and hatred of deeds done outside the Imam's authority
key_terms.ضال متحير: Straying and confused — the spiritual state of one without divine guidance
key_terms.ميتة كفر ونفاق: Death of disbelief and hypocrisy — dying outside the fold of true Islam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about worshipping without a divinely appointed Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delivers a powerful teaching to Muhammad ibn Muslim about the absolute necessity of following a divinely appointed Imam. Through a vivid parable of a lost sheep — wandering without its shepherd, deceived by strange flocks, and ultimately devoured by a wolf — the Imam illustrates the spiritual fate of those who worship God intensely but without the guidance of a legitimate Imam. The teaching culminates in a stark warning: dying without a manifest, just Imam from God is dying in the state of disbelief and hypocrisy, and the works of tyrannous imams and their followers are as scattered as ashes in a storm.
